recommendations:
TOP RESTAURANTS
Le Bernardin, Seafood, $120-$200 (INR 9000-15000), must-order Pan-Seared Scallops.
Per Se, Fine Dining, $100-$180 (INR 7500-13500), must-order Foie Gras.
Peruvian Place, Peruvian, $20-$40 (INR 1500-3000), must-order Ceviche.
Sushi Yasuda, Japanese, $50-$100 (INR 3750-7500), must-order Omakase.
Eleven Madison Park, French, $150-$250 (INR 11250-18750), must-order Seasonal Tasting Menu.

TOP ATTRACTIONS
Statue of Liberty, iconic landmark and symbol of freedom, best time to go is early morning, entry fee $21.50 (INR 1625).
Central Park, scenic green space in the middle of Manhattan, best time to go is afternoon, entry fee free.
Metropolitan Museum of Art, world-class art museum, best time to go is morning, entry fee $25 (INR 1875).
9/11 Memorial & Museum, historic site and tribute to victims, best time to go is late afternoon, entry fee $24 (INR 1800).
Brooklyn Bridge, iconic bridge with great city views, best time to go is sunset, entry fee free.

HIDDEN GEMS
The Little Red Lighthouse, a small historic lighthouse under the George Washington Bridge.
Morris-Jumel Mansion, a historic mansion with beautiful gardens.
New York Earth Room, an indoor sculpture featuring 280,000 pounds of dirt.

TRAVEL TIPS
Be respectful of local customs by tipping at least 15% in restaurants.
Use the subway as the best transport option, with a single ride costing $3 (INR 225).
Avoid common scams like overpriced street vendors and fake ticket sellers.
Useful phrases include "excuse me" and "thank you", which are "excuse me" and "dhanyavad" in Hindi.
Be aware of pickpocketing in crowded areas and keep valuables secure.

SHOPPING
Fifth Avenue, designer clothing and luxury goods, price range $50-$1000 (INR 3750-75000).
Brooklyn Flea, vintage items and street food, price range $10-$50 (INR 750-3750).
Grand Central Market, local produce and specialty foods, price range $10-$30 (INR 750-2250).
